title: The healthcare voice agent landscape in 2026
summary: 127 healthcare voice AI companies sorted by who the agent talks to: patients, providers, payers, plan members, pharmacies or developers. 16 call the payer. 14 were founded in 2025 or 2026.
body_markdown:
Voice AI is the loudest corner of healthcare software right now. We wanted to know who is on the phone, and to whom. The result is a[sortable list of 127 companies](https://asteroid.ai/market-maps/voice-ai) .


## Who the agent talks to


Every company is tagged with the party on the other end of the line:


- Patients: 93 companies. Scheduling, intake, reminders, refills, follow-up.
- Providers: 33, mostly agents that take a call from a referring office or a clinic.
- Plan members: 23, answering for the health plan.
- Payers: 16. Agents that sit on hold with the insurer for eligibility, auth status and claim status.
- Pharmacies: 10.
- Developers: 16 infrastructure vendors that sell the stack the others are built on.


Filter by any of those, by segment, or by direction. Sort by founding year or by funding.


## What the data says


The wave is front-office. 30 of the 90 dated companies were founded in 2024 or later, and almost all of them answer the practice phone.


Few call the payer. Sixteen companies on the whole map call the insurer. It is the slowest call in healthcare and the one with the least patience for small talk.


Consolidation has started. TrueLark went to Weave, Parlance to Volaris, Opkit to 11x, TrampolineAI to Voicegain. We marked the moves in the detail rows.


## What happens after the call


When the agent hangs up, what it learned has to land in the EHR, the practice management system or the payer portal. Most of those have no API. Browser agents close that gap, which is why we keep this list.
